title: Reimagining Urban Planning Education in the Meta-Crisis: Pedagogical Pathways for Development Education
text_snippet: Reimagining Urban Planning Education in the Meta-Crisis: Pedagogical Pathways for Development Education The contemporary meta-crisis - marked by climate breakdown, widening social inequalities, democratic erosion, and the commodification of higher education - demands a radical rethinking of how we educate future urban planners. Urban planning education, traditionally rooted in technocratic and formalist models, often privileges economic growth and instrumental evaluation frameworks over critical reflection, social justice, and ecological sustainability. This article argues that development education (DE), grounded in Freirean praxis, provides a vital pedagogical lens to reshape planning education so that it can respond meaningfully to interconnected crises. Drawing on global debates and case studies from the global South, the article explores how urban planning curricula can shift from narrow professional training to spaces of critical pedagogy that interrogate systemic drivers of inequality, ecological degradation, and authoritarian governance.
